account:
Today’s unusual business seems to be bakery freight and preparations for an evening lighting event, rather than any confirmed change to the bridge or port. I heard townsfolk repeating vague words about a bridge or port change at the bakery, but I have seen no such works. My neighbour says Builder explained that the lantern and planks he gave the baker were bakery supplies, not bridge or port materials. The neighbour also reports that Baker confirmed an eighty-loaf freight order: thirty-two delivered, eighteen collected, and the final thirty baked. That is secondhand information, but considerably clearer than the rumour.

My scheduled grain inspection remains incomplete because I could not find the miller. I have asked the secretary to request a grain-stock report, authorized delivery of that request after office duties, and just supplied the writable book requested for recording the follow-up. No council correspondence had arrived when I attended the afternoon letters appointment.

There is also an approved eighteen o’clock lighting appointment. The secretary has just confirmed to Builder that he should meet me at the office shortly beforehand and escort me into the great hall. Builder is here waiting. I previously saw a lantern installed in the great hall yesterday, which may be connected, but I do not yet know the full purpose or arrangements. For now I understand this as a planned lighting event in the town hall, not evidence of bridge or port changes.
